practices.practice: Create and reuse a single MongoClient (process-wide singleton) instead of creating a client per request; initialize once (e.g., at startup) and reuse the connection pool.
practices.prior_belief: Create a single MongoClient at application startup and reuse it for all requests (instantiate in FastAPI startup event and close in shutdown) and tune maxPoolSize to match your concurrency rather than creating per-request clients.

practices.practice: Tune connection-pool parameters and timeouts to your environment: small pools and short maxIdleTimeMS for serverless, larger pools for long-running servers, and set connectTimeoutMS/socketTimeoutMS/serverSelectionTimeoutMS to avoid stuck requests.
practices.prior_belief: Configure sensible client timeouts to avoid stuck requests: set serverSelectionTimeoutMS, connectTimeoutMS and socketTimeoutMS appropriate to your network; don't rely on defaults that may hang under network partitions.

practices.practice: Always require TLS on client connections to Azure DocumentDB and do not disable certificate validation in production (fix CA bundle/SNI issues rather than using tlsAllowInvalidCertificates).
practices.prior_belief: Enforce TLS/SSL for all client connections (use mongodb+srv:// or ?tls=true in the URI) and validate server certificates (do not set tlsAllowInvalidCertificates); fail fast if TLS validation fails.

practices.practice: Keep connection strings and API keys out of source control: read DOCUMENTDB_URI and other secrets from environment variables locally and use a secret store (Key Vault / managed identities) for production.
practices.prior_belief: Keep the DocumentDB connection string and any API keys out of source control: read DOCUMENTDB_URI (and OPENAI_API_KEY) from environment variables in runtime, and use Azure Key Vault (or equivalent secret store) for production secrets instead of embedding them in files.

practices.practice: Enable the driver's retryable reads/writes and implement application-level exponential-backoff retries for transient errors (use retryReads/retryWrites and catch transient error codes to retry idempotent ops).
practices.prior_belief: Enable and rely on the driver's retryable writes and implement exponential-backoff retries for transient network or server errors (set retryWrites=true in the URI and catch transient exceptions to retry idempotent operations).

practices.practice: Create a compound index for common query shapes on event collections following the ESR rule (Equality → Sort → Range), e.g., a compound index on (customer_id ASC, event_time ASC) to support per-customer ordered scans.
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes that support the attribution aggregations: at minimum a compound index on (customer_id, event_time) (customer_id ASC, event_time ASC) and additional indexes on channel/source/type fields used for grouping or filtering.

practices.practice: Use TTL (expireAfterSeconds) indexes to implement retention policies for raw event collections so they don't grow unbounded; tune expireAfterSeconds for your compliance and analytics needs.
practices.prior_belief: Apply a data retention policy for raw events (for example a TTL index on event_time) so event collections don’t grow unbounded; tune expireAfterSeconds to your compliance and analytics needs.

practices.practice: When storing vectors, create a cosmosSearch vector index with the correct kind (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF), explicit dimensions, and similarity metric (COS/L2/IP); prefer DiskANN for production-scale workloads and ensure index parameters (maxDegree, lBuild) are tuned for the latency/recall tradeoff.
practices.prior_belief: When storing vectors, use a fixed-length float array field and create a dedicated vector index with an appropriate metric (cosine or L2) and HNSW/IVF parameters (e.g., m/efConstruction/efSearch) tuned for the latency/recall tradeoff; record the vector dimension in the schema for validation.

practices.practice: Normalize embeddings for cosine similarity and store embedding metadata (model name and dimension) alongside vectors so you can detect model drift and rebuild indexes when models change.

Use network isolation (Private Endpoint / firewall rules), prefer Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) and RBAC for application authentication, and enable customer-managed keys (CMK) for data-at-rest encryption on regulated workloads.
Validate heavy queries and index usage using explain('executionStats') (or MCP explain_operation) and iterate indexes based on explain plans and index-stats before deploying changes.
practices.prior_belief: Validate heavy queries and index usage using explain() and the provider’s management/inspection tools (the documentdb MCP tools) before deploying; iterate indexes based on actual explain plans.

practices.practice: For local development use the DocumentDB Gateway image (MongoDB protocol on port 10260), keep local TLS relaxation strictly local (tlsAllowInvalidCertificates only for developer containers), and drive relaxation from environment variables so production code never disables verification.

Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logging, and alert on CPU, memory, IOPS, storage and connection-saturation metrics (integrate with Azure Monitor / Log Analytics) to detect regressions and high load.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and emit operational metrics (query latencies, aggregation durations, index hit rates, connection pool metrics) and integrate with Azure Monitor/alerts so you detect regressions in throughput or slow attribution runs.

practices.practice: Maintain an index budget (keep the number of indexes modest, e.g., 5–15), review $indexStats and drop or hide unused indexes using a hide→verify→drop lifecycle.

Shard collections only when a collection's storage or throughput exceeds a single physical shard's budget; choose the shard key based on workload (read-heavy → frequent query filter; write-heavy → high-cardinality evenly-distributed field) and avoid hot keys.
Enforce idempotency at ingestion with a unique index on the ingestion identifier (e.g., event_id or customer_id+event_id) so repeated ingestion attempts don't create duplicates.
practices.prior_belief: Enforce idempotency for event ingestion by using an event_id and a unique index on event_id (or on customer_id+event_id) so repeated seed/rerun operations don't create duplicates.

practices.practice: When reading large event sets, use server-side pagination (cursors + limit+sort) and reasonable batchSize rather than loading entire collections into memory.
practices.prior_belief: Use server-side pagination and reasonable batchSize settings when reading large event sets for attribution (use cursors/limit+sort rather than loading entire collections into memory).

practices.practice: When changing indexes in production, hide or test an index first, verify the winning plan and performance, then drop the old index to avoid accidental regressions.

Pick storage and compute tiers to match I/O and throughput needs (size compute for IOPS/throughput and storage for capacity; e.g., Premium SSD v2 decouples IOPS from disk size so size compute for performance).

When using agent tools (MCP) never paste connection strings into chat, never log or echo credentials, and store DocumentDB connection profiles in MCP configuration (CONNECTION_PROFILES) rather than passing raw secrets to agents.
Use the provider's vector-index memory-reduction features (product quantization, fp16) when indexing very large embedding sets to lower RAM while accepting a controlled recall tradeoff.
Record schemaVersion on documents to support lazy schema migration and safe forward evolution of attribution/result documents.
When diagnosing slow queries, gather explain output, index stats, collection stats and sample documents (via MCP or mongosh) before recommending index or schema changes.
Prefer Azure DocumentDB's dedicated full-text search (`createSearchIndexes` + $search) for lexical search scenarios instead of the community `$text` index.

When using serverless functions, initialize the MongoClient outside the handler so warm containers reuse the pool and set small maxPoolSize/minPoolSize and short maxIdleTimeMS appropriate to the function instance model.
Before changing indexes in production, check the collection's index count and warn if many indexes exist; prefer one well-designed compound index to many overlapping single-field indexes.
When changing embedding models or index similarity/dimensions, rebuild the vector index; mismatched dimensions or similarity produce silently-incorrect results.
When using MCP, prefer TRANSPORT=stdio for local use and set AUTH_REQUIRED=false only for stdio; never expose unauthenticated HTTP transports without Entra protection.

When diagnosing connection problems, check networking allowlist/firewall, private endpoint configuration, SNI/TLS settings and ensure the connection string includes tls=true and properly URL-encoded credentials.
When creating indexes on a sharded collection, ensure an index exists on the shard key and consider enableLargeIndexKeys if needed; resharding is possible but costly for large collections.

If you need atomic version increments, prefer single-document atomic updates where possible but the public Azure DocumentDB docs do not prescribe a single canonical pattern for multi-version documents across the service.
practices.prior_belief: Store attribution results as single per-customer documents and implement versioning with an incrementing version number updated atomically via findOneAndUpdate (or $inc) and enforce uniqueness with a compound unique index on (customer_id, version).

practices.practice: The public Azure DocumentDB guidance does not contain a clear recommendation that multi-document transactions should be avoided for cost/latency reasons; specific transactional trade-offs for multi-document transactions are not documented in the installed guidance.
practices.prior_belief: Prefer single-document atomic updates (upserts / findOneAndUpdate) for versioned writes to avoid multi-document transactions; only use multi-document transactions when absolutely necessary because of cost/latency.
practices.how_found: azure documentdb multi-document transactions cost guidance; azure documentdb transactions best practices

practices.practice: The installed Azure DocumentDB guidance does not expose a service-level recommendation about tuning writeConcern/readConcern (w/wtimeoutMS) for application durability vs latency; explicit writeConcern tuning guidance was not found in the searched DocumentDB materials.
practices.prior_belief: Set appropriate writeConcern/readConcern for attribution writes: use w='majority' (and a sensible wtimeoutMS) if you need durability across replicas; relax to w=1 for lower latency when acceptable.
practices.how_found: azure documentdb writeConcern w majority guidance; azure documentdb readConcern guidance

practices.practice: I could not find provider guidance that explicitly recommends using mongomock vs a dedicated test database for Azure DocumentDB; the installed docs discuss local Gateway and test parity but do not prescribe test-framework choices.
practices.prior_belief: For tests and local development use mocks or a separate test database (mongomock for unit tests and a dedicated test database on the cluster for integration tests); never run test seed scripts against production data.
practices.how_found: azure documentdb testing recommendations mongomock; azure documentdb test environment best practices

practices.practice: I found no explicit Azure DocumentDB guidance that mandates redaction or hashing of PII in logs as a service-specific requirement; general security best-practices exist but no service-specific doc was located in the skills searched.
practices.prior_belief: Redact or avoid persisting sensitive PII in logs and consider hashing or tokenizing customer identifiers when storing or exporting attribution data for analytics to meet privacy requirements.
practices.how_found: azure documentdb PII logging guidance; azure documentdb data protection logging best practices

practices.prior_belief: Protect the LangChain/OpenAI integration: require OPENAI_API_KEY in env, validate presence at startup, never log the key, and implement rate-limiting and per-user quota controls for marketer-facing natural-language queries.
